Reusable collections work. Live at **http://maker:4001/collections.html** (screenshot `prototypes/shot-58-collections-applied.png`).

**What a collection is** — a saved combination of **search text + tags to include + tags to exclude**, kept by name in a **Collections** list on the left. Here I've opened **"Reading, no desserts"**: it includes `#reading` (green) and excludes `−#dessert` (red), and instantly shows the 3 matching bookmarks (the Reading article, Rust, and the Rome book — the chocolate tart is excluded).

**Building and saving one** — you set the search text, add **Include tags** (a bookmark must have *all* of them) and **Exclude tags** (hide any that carry them), name it, and **Save as collection**. The tag fields use the same as-you-type suggestions as everywhere else, so your tag names stay consistent. Clicking a saved collection re-applies it; saving over the same name updates it.

**Crucially, collections are *live*, not frozen** — the count line notes it *"updates automatically as you save new matching bookmarks."* So "Reading, no desserts" always reflects whatever currently matches, rather than a fixed snapshot of items.

A few things to confirm:

1. Is a collection being **live/dynamic** (always shows current matches) what you want — as opposed to a fixed list of the bookmarks that matched when you saved it?
2. I split tags into explicit **Include (must have all)** and **Exclude** fields, plus free text. Does that match how you think about defining one — and is **"include = must have ALL"** right, or would you sometimes want "has *any* of these"?
3. Should a collection also be able to **pin a status or sort** (e.g. "only To read, sorted oldest"), or keep collections purely about text + tags?
